sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface labeling confirmed by fluorophore attachment prior to lysis; di-heteromer formation with GluK1 detected. Functional electrophysiology not explicitly reported for this construct in the cited clip.
sites.rationale: The signal peptide spans residues 1-31 (landmark-authoritative); an N-terminal tag must be inserted after residue 31 so it is not cleaved with the signal peptide. The FLAG-CLIP tag was placed at the N-terminus of full-length GluK2 and confirmed at the cell surface by pre-lysis fluorophore labeling (L1, L2). Because the paper names no specific residue number but the topology leaves exactly one extracellular N-terminus, position_evidence is topology_derived and insert_after_residue=31 is the unique valid junction. Residue 31 is G and residue 32 is T, copied from the numbered sequence. FLAG-CLIP-GluK2 full-length construct expressed in HEK cells; co-expressed with HA-SNAP-GluK1 and labeled with cell-impermeant fluorophores prior to lysis, confirming surface display of the N-terminally tagged receptor.

sources.claim: To enable investigation of GluK1/K2 di-heteromers, we generated a GluK2 construct with an N-terminal FLAG epitope followed by a CLIP tag for attachment to benzylcytosine-conjugated (BC) fluorophores.
We utilized the RUSH system by tagging the GluK2 KAR subunit and both the GluA1 and GluA2 AMPAR subunits at the N terminus with a streptavidin-binding peptide (SBP) and a fluorescent tag.

We first validated the APEGS assay by expressing YFP-myc-GluK2 wild-type (GluK2-WT) or a double cysteine mutant C858/C871A (GluK2-C2A), which has previously been reported to be non-palmitoylatable in cell lines ( Pickering et al., 1995 ; Copits and Swanson, 2013 ), in HEK293T cells.

The Halo-tag cDNA was inserted into the pCAGGS expression vector before GluA2 flip (Q)-3′UTR. cDNAs of rat GluK2(Q) was subcloned into the pCAGGS vector, and 2xHA-tag was inserted into downstream of the signal peptide of rat GluK2(Q).

literature_notes: All four ledger-supported sites map to the same physical junction (after residue 31, the end of the signal peptide) because GRIK2 has a cleaved signal peptide and the extracellular N-terminus is the only accessible N-terminal surface position. They are reported as four separate entries because they derive from four independent publications using four different tag types (FLAG+CLIP, SBP+EGFP+myc, YFP+myc, 2xHA), each grounded in a distinct ledger line. No ledger line supports any internal extracellular loop insertion or the second extracellular domain (residues 660-819). The second extracellular segment (660-819, between TM2 and TM3) is topologically accessible but no ledger evidence supports a tag there.
